19404.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6675 : Digital Design and Construction { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Current industry scenarios - its struggles and challenges, BIM Acronym? What problems do we face with 2D CAD? BIM as a collaborative process, BIM Characteristics, Benefits, Barriers and its misconception.
Module 2 :

BIM Dimensions, BIM Adoption status and country-wise implementation guidelines, and BIM stakeholders’ roles and responsibilities, Maturity Levels, LoD, Integrated Model.
Module 3 :

BIM Strategic Alignment and Implementation (execution plan, information requirements, delivery plan, etc.).
Module 4 :

BIM Enabled Sustainability, BIM for Construction Health and Safety, BIM for infrastructure projects, BIM for Facility and Asset management.
Module 5 :

Basics about interoperability, Common Data Environment, Export formats and applications, exchange of information through IFC, COBie, Open BIM, BIM 360, Digital Twin, Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, Mixed Reality applications in construction.
Module 6 :

Creating 3D building models- Project creation and settings, use of grids, levels, and units, to create – site/plot plan, footing details.
Module 7 :

Creating columns, compound wall, railings, etc. Switch windows, to create – ground floor, external and internal walls, etc.
Module 8 :

Creating Staircase and remaining floors, copy clipboard, etc., shaft openings, use of doors, windows, hardware, and other inbuilt families, etc.
Module 9 :

Dynamic linking, 3D views, and Rendering, Auto Elevations and sections, Sheet composition, etc.
Module 10 :

Use of an integrated model, BIM for coordination and RFI generation, 3D clash detection, 4D simulation, 5D quantification, etc.

Course Objective

1 .

To provide students with an understanding of the digital design and construction concept holistically.
2 .

To demonstrate skills related to object-based modelling.
3 .

To demonstrate a model-based collaboration process.
4 .

To introduce the AEC industry's most recent BIM advancements.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to understand the digital design and construction concept holistically.
2 .

Students will be able to understand recent developments in digital design and construction.
3 .

Students will be able to develop BIM objects and a project.
4 .

Students will be able to develop an integrated BIM model and identify and resolve clashes in the digital model.
5 .

Students will be able to understand and learn advanced BIM applications in Architecture, Engineering, and the Construction Industry.

6348.t: CH6301: Modeling and Analysis of Energy Systems
6348.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH6301 : Modeling and Analysis of Energy Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-1
Basic system modelling concepts: state variables, energy and mass balances, simulation parameters and equations, degree of freedom analysis, different types of specifications, inequalities, objective functions. Energy systems models: steps in model development, steady state and dynamic, lumped and distributed parameter models, Modeling and similitude
Module-II
Numerical methods and their implications, Sequential or simultaneous solving approach, Qualitative techniques - curve-fitting, regression analysis
Module-III
Mathematical models for energy systems (Heat Transfer equipment and Fluid flow), models resulting in algebraic equations, ODE (initial value and boundary value), and PDE
Module-IV
Performance and analysis of energy systems: Case studies
Module-V
Optimization: decision variables, objective functions and constraints, solving strategies, Unconstrained problems- necessary and sufficiency conditions, Constrained optimization- Lagrange multipliers, constrained variations, Kuhn-Tucker conditions, Linear Programming, pivoting, sensitivity analysis Search Techniques- Univariate/Multivariate. Case studies of optimization in Energy systems problems.

Course Objective

1 .

To develop skills in modeling energy systems using various tools and techniques.
2 .

To model and analyze complex energy systems
3 .

To optimize energy systems for improved efficiency and reduced environmental impact

Course Outcome

1 .

After learning the course the student must be able to:
1. To understand the steps in model development for different energy systems.
2. To scale up the process using similitude and dimensional analysis.
3. To develop energy system models resulting in algebraic equations, ODE and PDE .
4. To apply numerical methods to estimate the performance of energy models .
5. To understand solution strategies while optimizing the variables of a process.

Essential Reading

1 .

K. M. Hangos and I. T. Cameron,, Process Modeling and Model Analysis, Academic Press , 2001

2 .

T. F. Edgar, D. M. Himmelblau and L. S. Lasdon, Optimization of Chemical Processes, McGraw Hill, New York, , 2001

Supplementary Reading

1 .

W. L. Luyben,, Process Modelling, Simulation and Control for Chemical Engineers, McGraw Hill Book Co., New York , 2nd Ed

2 .

Bruce A. Finlayson, Introduction to Chemical Engineering Computing, Wiley , 2010

6092.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CS6303 : Information Theory and Coding { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

UNIT-I
Information theory: Concept of amount of information, information units Entropy: marginal, conditional, joint and relative entropies, relation among entropies Mutual information, information rate, channel capacity, redundancy and efficiency of channels Discrete channels – Symmetric channels, Binary Symmetric Channel, Binary Erasure Channel, Noise-Free Channel, Channel with independent I/O, Cascaded channels, repetition of symbols, Binary asymmetric channel, Shannon theorem
UNIT-II
Source coding – Encoding techniques, Purpose of encoding, Instantaneous codes, Construction of instantaneous codes, Kraft’s inequality, Coding efficiency and redundancy, Source coding theorem. Construction of basic source codes – Shannon Fano coding, Shannon Fano Elias coding, Huffman coding, Minimum variance Huffman coding, Adaptive Huffman coding, Arithmetic coding, Dictionary coding – LZ77, LZ78, LZW, ZIP coding Channel coding, Channel coding theorem for DMC
UNIT-III
Codes for error detection and correction – Parity check coding, Linear block codes, Error detecting and correcting capabilities, Generator and Parity check matrices, Standard array and Syndrome decoding, Hamming codes Cyclic codes – Generator polynomial, Generator and Parity check matrices, Encoding of cyclic codes, Syndrome computation and error detection, Decoding of cyclic codes, BCH codes, RS codes, Burst error correction
UNIT-IV
Convolutional codes – Encoding and State, Tree and Trellis diagrams, Maximum likelihood decoding of convolutional codes -Viterbi algorithm, Sequential decoding -Stack algorithm. Interleaving techniques – Block and convolutional interleaving, Coding and interleaving applied to CD digital audio system - CIRC encoding and decoding, interpolation and muting. ARQ – Types of ARQ, Performance of ARQ, Probability of error and throughput

Course Objective

1 .

To define and apply the basic concepts of information theory (entropy, channel capacity etc.)
2 .

To learn the principles and applications of information theory in communication systems
3 .

To study various data compression methods and describe the most common such methods
4 .

To understand the theoretical framework upon which error-control codes are built

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students shall be equipped with the knowledge to:
CO1: quantify the notion of information, entropy, channel capacity in a mathematically sound way and understand its significance in the communications systems.
CO2: differentiate between lossy and lossless compression techniques and decide an efficient data compression scheme for a given information source.
CO3: design communication systems with error control capabilities.

Essential Reading

1 .

T. M. Cover, J. A. Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Wiley

2 .

S. Lin, D.J. Costello, Error Control Coding: Fundamentals and Applications, Pentice-Hall

Supplementary Reading

1 .

R. J. McEliece, The Theory of Information and Coding, Cambridge Uinversity Press

2 .

R. Bose, Information Theory Coding and Cryptography, Tata McGraw Hill

19148.t: ME6311: Conduction and Radiation Heat Transfer
19148.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6311 : Conduction and Radiation Heat Transfer { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Recapitulation of the basic idea of 1D steady-state heat conduction and constant cross-section fin problems. [4 hours]
Module 2 :

Fundamental analysis and variables of the varying cross-sectional straight and circumferential fins. Derivation of generalized conduction equation for anisotropic inhomogeneous solids, conductive tensor, concepts of isotropic and homogeneous conductivity. Algebra of the indicial notations to represent the generalized conduction equation. [8 hours]

Module 3 :

Analytical solutions of the steady-state higher-dimensional conduction in solids with the simple and complex boundary conditions and heat generation. [7 hours]
Module 4 :

Analysis of heat conduction in a lumped system, transient conduction in simple systems, and transient heat conduction with complex boundaries. [7 hours]
Module 5 :

Recapitulation of fundamentals of radiative heat transfer, radiative properties of surfaces, methods of estimating configuration factors, heat exchange between diffusively emitting and diffusively reflecting surfaces. Radiative energy transfers by absorbing and emitting two distinctly located real surfaces. Combined conduction and radiation systems. [8 hours]

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the scopes of generalized heat conduction in anisotropic, inhomogeneous
material with the complex boundary conditions
2 .

To solve the realistic fin problems of varying cross-sectional straight and annular fins.
3 .

To solve analytically the problem of higher-dimensional steady/unsteady heat conduction.
4 .

To determine and solve the problems of radiative heat flux between the two surfaces.

Course Outcome

1 .

To study the generalized heat conduction equations and complex boundary conditions.

2 .

To solve analytically the realistic fin problems of varying cross-sectional straight and annular fins.

3 .

To determine the analytical solutions of 1-D, 2D, and higher steady-state conduction temperature distribution and heat transfer rate.
4 .

To determine the analytical solutions of the lumped system,1-D, and higher transient conduction temperature distribution and heat transfer rate.
5 .

To determine the radiative heat flux between the two surfaces with a participating/non-participating medium.

Essential Reading

1 .

Arpaci, V.S. and Arpaci, V.S., Conduction heat transfer, MA: Addison-Wesley , 2020

2 .

Modest, M.F. and Mazumder, S., Radiative heat transfer., Academic press , 2021

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Hahn, D.W. and Özisik, M.N, Heat conduction., John Wiley & Sons , 2022

2 .

Kraus, A.D., Aziz, A., Welty, J. and Sekulic, D.P, Extended surface heat transfer, Wiley Publications. , 2021

Journal and Conferences

1 .

Ma, C.C. and Chang, S.W., 2004. Analytical exact solutions of heat conduction problems for anisotropic multi-layered media. International journal of heat and mass transfer, 47(8-9), pp.1643-1655.
2 .

Burggraf, O.R., 1964. An exact solution of the inverse problem in heat conduction theory and applications.

8652.t: PA5418: Hospital Planning and Design Principles
8652.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA5418 : Hospital Planning and Design Principles { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I: Introduction to Healthcare Planning and Design:Important Definitions and Concepts related to Healthcare Architecture, Evolution of Healthcare facilities concerning Human Settlements in Indian and International contexts, Types and Levels of Healthcare Delivery systems in India. Classification of Hospitals based on Bed Size or Capacity, Specialty, System of Medicine, Administration, ownership, or control, etc. Introduction to Various Hospital Planning Guidelines and Standards-Indian and International.
Module II: Healthcare Planning and Design: Major Functional Divisions of the Hospital and Hospital Site Planning Principles.Different Typologies of Hospital Design- Balancing Form and Function in Healthcare Designs Major components/divisions of a hospital's main Functional Departments, Ancillary and Support Departments, Hospital Administrative departments, and Hospital Engineering Departments.
Hospital Space and Area Programming, Hospital Grid Design, Manpower, Beds, and Resource Planning criteria for Healthcare Facilities as per IS codes, Indian Health Facility Guidelines(iHFG), and Indian Public Health Standards, Hospital Site Planning Principles and Site Selection Criteria.
Module III: Design Considerations for the Main Functional Units of a Hospital:
Key Planning Parameters and Detailed Design Considerations for: The Outpatient Department (OPD) and its inter-relationship with other departments of the Hospital
The Central Diagnostic Department (Central Laboratory and Central Imaging facility) and its inter-relationship with other departments of the HospitalThe In-Patient Department (IPD., Critical and Non-Critical Units) and its inter-relationship with other departments of the HospitalThe Emergency Department (ED) and its inter-relationship with other departments of the Hospital The Operation Room Complex (OR-Complex) and its inter-relationship with other departments of the Hospital.
Module III: Design Considerations for the Ancillary and Support Departments and Administrative Departments of the Hospital:Key Planning Parameters and detailed design considerations for the Ancillary and Support Departments and their inter-relationship with other departments of the Hospital, e.g., CSSD, Central Pharmacy, Blood Bank, Central Dietary Department, Hospital Laundry, Mortuary/Morgue, Central Housekeeping and Maintenance Department, Gas Manifold Room and Biomedical Waste Management Unit, etc.
Key Planning Parameters and detailed design considerations for the Hospital Administrative Departments and their inter-relationship with other departments of the Hospital.
Module-IV: Outcome-based Healthcare Design Concepts and Design of Speciality Hospitals:Design Concepts related to Evidence-Based Healthcare Design, Salutogenic Hospital design, Optimal Healing Environment Design, and Biophilic Design Design considerations for Specialised Hospitals (e.g., Teaching Hospitals, Oncology hospitals, Orthopaedic and Cardiac Care Institutes, other multi-specialty Hospitals, etc.)

Course Objective

1 .

To develop a fundamental understanding of healthcare facilities at secondary and tertiary levels.
2 .

To acquire knowledge to blend technical, functional, and aesthetic requirements into an architectural design
3 .

To understand the key planning parameters and design considerations for various functional components/ divisions(departments) of the hospital and the interrelationships between them
4 .

To understand the latest Outcome-based Healthcare Design Concepts and their incorporation into the Functional Architectural design of healthcare facilities.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to provide a functional design for a hospital that ensures efficient, safe, and appropriate spaces for patients, their families, and the staff.
2. Ability to generate a zone-wise distribution of various departments of the hospital, establishing the necessary required inter-departmental connectivity.
3. Ability to generate and integrate space and area programming, resource and manpower planning, design considerations, and key planning parameters of various departments into a functional design of the hospital.
4. Ability to generate efficient site circulation with a clear segregated path for site-related traffic (users, material and vehicle.)
5. Ability to design healthcare spaces with the incorporation of Outcome-based Healthcare Design Concepts to create healing and restorative environments for the users.

Essential Reading

1 .

Garg, A., & Dewan, A. (2022)., Manual of Hospital Planning and designing: For medical administrators, architects and planners, Springer

2 .

Gupta, A. K. (2007)., Modern trends in planning and designing of Hospitals Principles and Practice., Jaypee Brothers Publishers.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Ministry of Family and Welfare (2022), Indian Public Health Standards Sub District Hospital and District Hospital, Volume-1., Ministry of Family and Welfare (2022)

2 .

Kunders, G. D., Gopinath, S., & Katakam, A. (1998)., Hospitals: Planning, design, and Management., Tata, McGraw-Hill.
